lesson: A load-bearing guard is the last place a widened class gets noticed. The unusable-situs rule was widened in three files and narrowed in the one that gated the envelope request body, so the defect surfaced as 'the map drew nothing' three layers away from the actual bug. Where a predicate decides whether to KEEP an input rather than whether to reject it, four copies is one bug waiting for a divergence.

A predicate that answers 'is this string usable' and a predicate that answers 'must I drop this input' are different predicates. Merging them in the drop-guard's direction would have regressed the truncated-ZIP tail ("17006 DASHWOOD CREEK DR, TX 7866" is a well-formed street line that isUsableSitusAddress deliberately passes and the geocoder cannot match). The wider drop rule is the UNION, not the substitution — and the surviving test for the truncated-ZIP case is what proves it.

The card's four-state facet vocabulary reads as the customer's truth, so 'absent' with no message is a claim. Over a parcel the county plainly addressed, a blank was a false claim of the same kind as the wrong sentence it replaced.
deadEnd: `git show HEAD:<path> > <file>` under PowerShell redirection corrupts the file (adds a BOM / re-encodes), so a revert-and-run through that route fails as 'invalid JS syntax' from vite rather than reproducing pre-fix behaviour. Copy to a temp file and make the targeted edit instead. Cost: one wasted 70s run.

A PowerShell here-string passed as `git commit -m $msg` breaks git's argv on any quote inside the message ('pathspec ... did not match any file(s)'). Write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
Do not scope `rg` or a recursive Get-ChildItem to all of P: — it runs for minutes and starves the install running beside it. Scope to the clone.
`pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in hauska-map takes 7m35s on P:. Budget for it; it is not hung.
